Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Which city office sends the bill

The Collector of Revenue sends it, and the Assessor decides what the house is worth. St. Louis stands apart from any county, so these two City Hall offices do the jobs that a county treasurer and county assessor handle elsewhere in Missouri. Both work out of 1200 Market Street.

For valuation questions, the Assessor's real estate staff answer at (314) 622-4185 and assessor-real-estate@stlouis-mo.gov, in Room 120, weekdays from eight in the morning to five in the afternoon. Payments are taken in Room 109. The same Collector also bills personal property tax, earnings tax and water-refuse charges, so a house seller may hear from that office about more than one account.

The Collector tracks about 220,000 parcels, and the Assessor revalues them in odd-numbered years.

The city housing market

The city is home to an estimated 278,144 people, down 7.7% from the April 2020 base. Owners live in only 45.3% of homes, so rentals make up most of the housing stock. That matters if your property has a tenant. The median owner-reported home value is $197,500, median rent is $997 and median household income is $56,160. The city covers 61.74 square miles of land.

Owners with a mortgage report monthly costs near $1,487 in the middle, while those without a loan report $574. Set those figures beside the bill on your own parcel. A tax line that looks heavy next to them is a reason to prepare an appeal before May 1 arrives.

Due date, penalties and how to pay

Interest and a penalty begin on January 1. The Collector charges a single 2% penalty, then 2% interest each month, topping out at 18% for the year, and the interest keeps building each year until the balance is cleared. If more than one year is owed, the oldest year gets paid first.

Notices go out in November. Where a lender escrows the tax, the bill goes to the lender instead of you. If nothing shows up in your mailbox, the Assessor may hold an old address for you, or the deed may have changed hands after the bills were printed. Every bill can be viewed online. Address changes go through the Assessor in City Hall Room 114.

Ways to pay a St. Louis real estate tax bill
Payment optionWhereNotes
Online or phone appPayIt St. Louis accountWeb or mobile
In personRoom 109, Monday to FridayCurrent-year bills by card, cash, check, money order or cashier's check; delinquent bills cannot be paid by check
MailCollector of Revenue, PO Box 66877, St. Louis, MO 63166-6877Check, money order or cashier's check
Phone(314) 408-6887Card payment

Between mid-October and December 31, night deposit boxes at four Commerce Bank branches also accept payments. A pre-pay program lets owners deposit money toward later bills.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your assessment

You have three stages. The informal stage opens May 1 and closes June 23. Send appeal@stlouis-mo.gov your parcel number or address, or phone 314-622-4185 and leave a message with the same details.

Bring proof of value: a purchase contract, an appraisal by an appraiser, sales of similar houses, photos of defects, and for rentals the income and expense figures.

  1. Informal review with an appraiser.
  2. Board of Equalization. The request must reach the Assessor by the second Monday in July, and the board sits from July to the last Saturday in August. Ask for the form at that number, by email, or at Room 120 in City Hall.
  3. State Tax Commission. The deadline is September 30 or 30 days after the board rules, whichever comes later. The commission wants a board appeal first, though newly bought property is one of a few exceptions.

A homeowner may represent themselves before the Commission. A commercial owner needs counsel. Under RSMo 138.060, the assessor's number carries no built-in presumption of accuracy, and for a city outside any county the assessor has to show that the value is no higher than market. If you pay while disputing, read RSMo 139.031 first.

When a parcel stays unpaid

The city files a suit, and the sale follows roughly twelve months later. The Sheriff's Office conducts the auction. A notice of each suit is published weekly, and the Collector posts a suit and sale schedule.

An owner can pay the suit in full or call 622-4101 about a Redemption Contract. Opening bids equal the amount in the sale notice's legal description. State law adds a notice step: RSMo 140.150 directs the collector to mail the recorded owner before delinquent land is advertised, and an owner who never receives the letter still owes the tax.

Relief for older or disabled owners

The state offers the Missouri Property Tax Credit Claim, which helps qualified seniors and people who are 100 percent disabled recoup part of the real estate tax or rent they paid. The ceiling is $1,100 for an owner who lives in the home and $750 for a renter, scaled to taxes or rent paid against household income. The state number is (573) 751-3505.

Tax-exempt status is a different track. The Assessor reviews each parcel, and the owner has to present convincing evidence that the use fits Article X, Section 6 of the Missouri Constitution and RSMo 137.100.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a house with tax still due

The balance gets paid out of your proceeds. A title company will search for liens, and a delinquent bill or a pending suit has to be cleared before the buyer can take clean title. Hand over the parcel number early so a payoff figure can be requested.

The Assessor's site also links to the Housing Conservation inspection for residential occupancy, a basic check for minimal interior code violations and minimum exterior standards. Ask the city whether that inspection touches your sale.

Before you list, collect the paperwork a title company will want: your parcel number, the latest tax bill, your loan payoff and any notice you have received from the Collector. If the bill was mailed to a lender or to an old address, check with the Assessor so the record shows where you can be reached. Ask for the payoff figure a few days before closing, because interest keeps building and the amount can change.

A cash buyer can close without a lender's appraisal, which may help if a suit has been filed and time is short, but the tax still has to be cleared through the Collector either way.

Frequently asked questions

Whom do I pay for St. Louis real estate tax?

The Collector of Revenue. Pay at 1200 Market Street, Room 109, through PayIt St. Louis, by mail to PO Box 66877, or by phone at (314) 408-6887.

What does a late bill cost?

One 2% penalty plus 2% interest every month, up to 18% a year, on the balance left after December 31. The interest keeps adding yearly until the account is paid.

Which dates matter for a value appeal?

Informal hearings run May 1 to June 23, and the Board of Equalization request is due the second Monday in July. Email appeal@stlouis-mo.gov or call 314-622-4185 to start.

Does the city have a county treasurer?

No. St. Louis belongs to no county, so the city Assessor and the city Collector of Revenue perform the work a county assessor and collector would elsewhere.

May I close on a sale while tax is overdue?

Yes. The unpaid amount comes out of the proceeds at the table, and the title company can request a payoff. After a suit is filed, the Collector at 622-4101 can discuss a Redemption Contract.

St. Charles, MO Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Missouri

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on St. Charles property tax?

Who sends the tax bill inside city limits

The county does. St. Charles city government sets its own rate, but the value comes from the county Assessor and the money goes to the county Collector, who mails one combined statement. Nobody at City Hall takes a real estate tax payment.

  • Value and classification: St. Charles County Assessor, 201 N. Second Street, 636-949-7425.
  • Bills and payments: St. Charles County Collector of Revenue, Suite 134 at the same address, 636-949-7470.
  • City rate questions: the city Finance Department. The City Council sets the actual rate each August.

After values change, the city also mails a projected tax liability notice. It is a forecast of what the new assessed value could mean for the coming year. It is not a bill, so send no money. Your real bill has a line for every district that taxes the address: state, county, school, fire, ambulance and library.

The city at a glance

St. Charles is the county seat, on the Missouri River northwest of downtown St. Louis. An estimated 72,561 people live here, in 30,362 households. About 68.0% own their homes, a typical owned home is valued at $298,700, typical rent is $1,251, and the median household earns $85,937. The average commute is 21.6 minutes.

Schools depend on the block. The City of St. Charles School District covers most of town, Francis Howell serves southern pockets, and Orchard Farm serves the north. Check the district named on your own bill before you describe the house to buyers.

The county calendar and your sale

County statements go out by December 1 and are payable through December 31. A payment that arrives in January adds penalty and interest. The Assessor revalues real estate in odd-numbered years, so 2027 is next, and notices go out in April.

A disputed value goes through the Assessor's informal hearing first, then the Board of Equalization, then the State Tax Commission. The board form is due at 5 p.m. on the second Monday of July, and the next one falls on July 12, 2027. The county asks owners to book the informal hearing within 10 days of the notice mailing date.

One more rule matters at the closing table. Whoever holds title when the year ends is responsible for that year's real estate tax, and buyer and seller commonly split it by proration at the sale. Ask the title company to show its math before you sign.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

City charges on the tax bill

Voters approved two small yearly charges that the county adds to real estate bills for houses inside the city. Each one reimburses repairs to the pipe between the house and the public line.

Pipe repair programs on a St. Charles city tax bill
ProgramYearly chargePaysUnits covered
Sewer lateral repair$2090% of the lowest of three bids, up to $7,500Up to 6
Residential water line insurance$12100% of the lowest of three bids, up to $3,000Up to 4

Enrollment is automatic with no opt-out, and houses outside the city boundary are excluded. The sewer program reaches the pipe from the exterior wall to the city main. The water program reaches the line between the meter (or first shut-off valve) and the exterior wall. Buyers with questions can call Public Works, or Collections and Billing at 636-949-3212 for the water line.

Seller disclosure required by the city

Every residential sale inside the city comes with a disclosure signed by the seller. Council passed Ordinance 23-062 on June 6, 2023, and the requirement began September 1, 2023, so it reaches any closing today.

The signed form is notarized at closing, and a copy is sent to the city through an online link. It does not need to be recorded. The form gives the incoming owner formal notice of city rules such as:

  • Building and sign permits and required inspections.
  • Recreational vehicle and boat parking and storage, fencing and property maintenance.
  • Solid waste collection, short term rentals and floodplain development.
  • Historic preservation districts, site plan and architectural review, and zoning restrictions.

Community Development at 636-949-3222 answers questions about the form. Add it to your closing checklist so it is not forgotten.

Repairs and rentals that need approval

Some projects do need a permit. The Building Division lists decks, additions, basement finishing, electrical or plumbing changes, a water heater or heating and air unit replacement, a new sewer lateral and fences taller than 6 feet. Painting, new flooring, a new faucet, roof shingles and siding replacement do not. Call 636-949-3227 to schedule an inspection.

Rentals have their own rules. Long term rentals need a residential occupancy inspection before the first tenant and between tenants. For short term rentals, a 2025 amendment limited new residential permits to the Extended Historic Preservation District and cut the cap to 0.15% of housing units, up to 48 residential units. The city is at that maximum and is not accepting new residential applications, and owners should call St. Charles County at 636-949-7900 about property tax effects. A buyer who plans a short term rental should check zoning first at 636-949-3222.

Exterior changes in the historic district need approval from the Historic Landmarks Preservation and Architectural Review Board.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Preparing the house and the paperwork

Before you list, collect repair records for the roof, cooling system and water heater. The Assessor checks structure measurements against building permits, and new construction is added to the rolls every year, so keep permits for any finished basement, deck or addition together. Those are the projects the Building Division says need one.

Then line up the closing items: the disclosure form, your tax payoff figure from the Collector, and the district named on your bill. A buyer who sees the paperwork ready is less likely to ask for a price cut over surprises.

Steps for a St. Charles seller

  1. Look up your parcel with the Assessor and compare the value with what similar houses nearby have sold for.
  2. Ask the Collector at 636-949-7470 for the balance on your account, and pay any overdue amount so the title company has a clean number.
  3. Fill out the city disclosure form and keep the Community Development number handy in case the buyer has questions.
  4. If the buyer plans to rent, tell them early about the occupancy inspection and the short term rental limits.
  5. At closing, read the proration line so you know how the current year's tax was divided.

A sale to a cash buyer follows the same disclosure and proration steps, but it usually moves faster because no lender's appraisal or approval is involved.

Frequently asked questions

Where do St. Charles residents send their real estate tax?

Pay the St. Charles County Collector of Revenue at 201 N. Second Street, by phone at 1-855-227-7840, or online at stcharlesmocollector.org. The city itself does not take real estate tax payments.

Is the projected tax notice from the city a bill?

No. The notice estimates possible liability after an assessment change, and owners should not send money. The real bill comes later in the year from the county.

Is the city disclosure mandatory on a St. Charles sale?

Yes, for residential closings inside the city after September 1, 2023. The seller signs, a notary acknowledges it at closing, and the city receives a copy.

Can a homeowner skip the sewer lateral charge?

No. Voters approved the program, so every eligible home inside the city limits pays the $20 yearly charge and is enrolled. The same is true of the $12 water line program.

What is the route for disputing a St. Charles assessment?

Ask the county Assessor for an informal hearing, then file with the Board of Equalization by 5 p.m. on the second Monday in July. The next deadline is July 12, 2027. Further appeal goes to the State Tax Commission.

Kansas City, MO Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Missouri
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Kansas City, MO Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Kansas City, MO Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Kansas City, MO Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Owe Kansas City Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Kansas City houses as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Kansas City property tax?
We buy Kansas City houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

Which county bills my Kansas City property?

The answer turns on where the house sits. Kansas City spreads over about 319 square miles in four counties: Jackson, Clay, Platte and Cass. The city sends no tax bill of its own. Each county assessor values the parcels, and the city's levy is folded into the county statement.

  • Jackson County: Collection Department, 816-881-3232.
  • Clay County: Collector, 816-407-3200.
  • Platte and Cass counties: find the county collector's official site and search by parcel number or address.

Look at your latest tax statement. The county printed on it is the office to call.

Kansas City's own levies

Kansas City charges five levies, each stated per $100 of assessed valuation. For 2024 they total $1.5291 for city purposes. School, library and other districts add theirs, so ask your collector for the full rate on your parcel.

City of Kansas City levies, tax year 2024
Levy2024 rate per $100
General purpose$0.5469
Health$0.3799
Health temporary$0.1672
Museum$0.0151
Debt service$0.4200

Under Missouri rules, residential property is assessed at 19 percent of true value, agricultural land at 12 percent, other real property at 32 percent and personal property at 33 1/3 percent. County assessors adjust real property values in odd-numbered years, which puts the next reassessment in 2027.

The Kansas City housing market in brief

Kansas City has 521,220 residents as of 2025 and 221,979 households. Owners hold 55.4% of homes. A median owner-occupied home is valued at $242,900, and median gross rent is $1,238.

No single school district serves the city. About 15 districts share it, so two houses a few blocks apart may be in different ones, and that shows up in the bill. Wind, hail and water damage are realistic repair items on an older house here. An owner facing both repairs and a tax balance can weigh an as-is sale.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Why a city levy can change from year to year

A Missouri constitutional amendment caps the total tax the city may collect in a fiscal year. Levies are set to bring in about what the city got the year before, and going beyond that takes a majority vote. New construction, new personal property and newly annexed areas fall outside the cap.

Every levy also has a ceiling. The general purpose levy can reach $1.0000 per $100 and was $0.5469 in 2024. The health levy has a $0.5000 maximum against $0.3799 charged. So reassessment can change your assessed value without changing the rate, and a rate can change while your value stays flat.

Paying Jackson County property tax

The 2026 bill must be paid in full by December 31, 2026. Recalculations from 2026 appeal decisions are suspended until January 2027, which means the bill still has to be paid on time. Any refund then comes automatically, and paying under protest is not needed to get one. If a mortgage company paid the bill, the refund goes back to the lender.

  • In person: Jackson County Courthouse, 415 E 12th Street in Kansas City, or the Truman Courthouse, 112 W Lexington Avenue in Independence, open weekdays 8 to 5.
  • Drop boxes at both courthouses close at midnight on December 31. Cash is not accepted in them.
  • By mail to the Jackson County Collector, postmarked December 31 or earlier.
  • Online at payments.jacksongov.org. E-check is $1.25. Cards are 2.75% of the bill plus $2 per transaction, all kept by the processor.

Partial payments on real property are accepted, though not online. Interest, penalties and fees build on the unpaid part after December 31. Seniors can split the county bill into four equal installments without penalty through the Senior Quad Payment Program. The Collection Department can tell you if your account qualifies.

How to appeal a Jackson County assessment

Value appeals go to the Board of Equalization, whose filing window closes each July. Call the Real Property Assessment Department at 816-881-3530, or email tpaASMT@jacksongov.org, for a notice or print summary of values and for the current filing date.

A board ruling can be taken further to the Missouri State Tax Commission, which has an online filing process of its own. Two points matter. A stipulated value signed with the Assessment Department cancels the board appeal and ends any Commission appeal. And a withdrawal has to be in writing, mailed to the board at 1300 Washington, Kansas City, MO 64106.

Paying under protest follows Missouri statute 139.031: full payment on time, plus a written statement of your grounds and the fair market value you claim. Protest payments go to Attn: Protest, P.O. Box 219747, Kansas City, MO 64121-9747. Protest funds are released every other month, so a refund tied to a value change usually arrives faster if you skip the protest.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Houses in Clay County

In Clay County the usual mailing date is mid-November. No bill on November 30? Phone the Collector, 816-407-3200. State law wants the money in by December 31 whether or not a bill ever reached you.

Late payments, meaning a postmark after December 31, bring a single 9% penalty and 1.5% interest per month on what is unpaid. Skip bank bill-pay: those checks often arrive without a postmark and are posted by the date written on them. Clay County charges nothing for debit cards or e-check, but credit cards cost 2.45%.

Selling with taxes owed

Start by writing down three things: the county, the parcel number and the bill year. Your title company uses them to ask the collector for a balance and settles it when the sale closes.

  1. Get the payoff on paper before signing, most of all when an older year is open alongside the current one.
  2. Check it against the draft settlement statement.
  3. Ask the title company to pay the collector from your proceeds.
  4. Hold on to receipts for any year you pay yourself.

Timing matters near year end. A late-year closing can fall ahead of the due date, so settle in the contract whether the seller's share is paid at the table or credited to the buyer. Jackson County's Collection Department (816-881-3232) and the Clay County Collector (816-407-3200) can each confirm a parcel's balance. A house in the Platte or Cass part of the city has its own collector to call.

Someone carrying back tax plus repair needs may prefer an as-is cash sale. No lender means no appraisal and no repair demands, and the title company still pays the tax out of the proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

Who bills property tax for a house in Kansas City, Missouri?

The county where the parcel sits. Kansas City spans Jackson, Clay, Platte and Cass counties, and the city levy rides on the county bill instead of arriving separately.

When is the 2026 Kansas City tax bill due?

December 31, 2026. In Jackson County the drop boxes close at midnight that day, and mailed payments need a postmark of that date or earlier.

When can I appeal my Jackson County value?

Through the Board of Equalization, with filings closing in July each year. Call 816-881-3530 for a value summary and the current date. The next reassessment is in 2027.

Do I have to pay under protest to get a refund in Jackson County?

No. Refunds from a value change are issued automatically. Paying under protest can slow them down, since protest funds are released every other month.

What is the Kansas City city property tax rate?

The city's combined 2024 levy was $1.5291 per $100 of assessed valuation. School and other district rates come on top of that, so ask your collector for the total on your parcel.

Springfield context for sellers

The biggest city in the Ozarks, Springfield had an estimated 169,847 people in July 2025 over roughly 82 square miles. Only 43.9% of homes are lived in by their owners, which leaves renters in the majority. A typical owner-reported home is valued at $177,700, rent in the middle is $964, and the median household brings in $49,311. The average trip to work is 17.6 minutes. With numbers like these, plenty of buyers are investors and plenty of sellers own a former or future rental.

Which office handles Springfield property tax

Greene County handles it, not City Hall. The job is divided three ways inside the county. One office puts a value on the house, another converts the levies into the yearly tax book, and the third sends the statement and accepts the money.

Greene County offices that touch a Springfield tax bill
OfficeWhat it doesWhere and phone
AssessorSets the value940 N. Boonville Avenue, Room 35; real estate line (417) 868-4101
Collector of RevenueMails bills, takes paymentRoom 109, Historic Courthouse; (417) 868-4036
County ClerkKeeps levy rates, serves the Board of Equalization(417) 829-6244

Counter hours at the Collector run 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, with holidays off. For any parcel, the county's Public Access website (updated nightly) lists the owner and the school and taxing districts.

Due date, penalties and ways to pay

Midnight on December 31 is the cutoff. The county's notice on the 2025 bills spelled out a 9 percent penalty plus 2 percent interest once that date passes, and told mailers that a bank check must carry a postmark of December 31 or sooner. Any balance becomes delinquent on January 1. Statements generally arrive around the middle of November. If yours has not come, write to collectorhelp@greenecountymo.gov.

  • Pay at CountyCollector.com, by mail, by phone, or at the Room 109 counter in the courthouse at 940 N. Boonville Avenue.
  • Processor charges are $1.00 for an e-check, 1.5 percent on a debit card and 2.3 percent on a credit card, with a $2.00 minimum.
  • A hallway drop box takes payments during business hours until year end.
  • When several years are owed, the oldest has to be cleared before any newer bill.

The office is closed on Thanksgiving Day and the Friday after, so plan any in-person payment for another week.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who pays when a house sells mid-year?

Property tax attaches to the parcel rather than the person, and the Collector will not divide a single bill between two owners. The closing company handles the split, giving the buyer a credit for the part of the year you owned. Find that credit on the settlement statement and read it before signing.

With an escrow account, the lender receives the statement. If the lender has not paid by mid-December, the bill is sent again to the owner with extra time. Paying off the loan does not require telling the Collector, though the Assessor's mailing address for you should be up to date.

  • Ask the title company for this year's balance and any older ones before you choose a closing date.
  • Check that the owner name in the Assessor's record matches the recorded deed.
  • Save the receipt, which you can download from the Collector's site after an online payment.

How to challenge your valuation

Every odd-numbered year the Assessor resets real estate values as of January 1, which puts the next full reassessment in 2027. Notices of changed value usually go out ahead of June (the second full week of May in 2025), and only owners whose value went up receive one.

  • Informal review. Call an appraiser on the dedicated phone lines named in the notice, or use the Assessor's informal appeal form for real property.
  • Board of Equalization. The County Clerk must receive your form by the second Monday in July.
  • State Tax Commission. This is the last stop, reachable at 573-751-2414.

The Board certifies corrections to the tax book at 9:00 a.m. on the second Tuesday of each month and hears formal July appeals in Room 212 of the Historic Courthouse. It can raise a value, lower it or leave it alone. Value is only part of the picture: the bill equals assessed value times the district levy, divided by 100, so a rising levy can increase a bill even when the value holds still.

Senior credit and tax sales

The county's Senior Tax Credit lowers real estate tax for eligible older homeowners. New applicants may enroll from January 2 to June 30, and an approved household stays in without yearly renewal unless ownership or occupancy changes. A delinquent real estate balance on June 30 removes a participant, and the credit never moves the December 31 deadline.

Falling behind can end in a tax sale. The county holds its auction at 10 a.m. on the fourth Monday of August in Room 212 of the Historic Courthouse. A parcel is eligible once two or more years are owed on May 1, and clearing the full balance ahead of the sale removes it from the list. A Notice of Impending Sale goes out in April, and from July 1 the office accepts only certified funds.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling while behind on tax

Call the Collector sooner rather than later for an exact payoff, since interest keeps changing the number. The title company needs it, and the amount comes out of your proceeds at the table. When a parcel is near the August sale list, a fast closing may beat a long listing period. Cash buyers do not wait on a lender, but compare any offer with what a listing would leave after agent fees and repairs.

Short-term rentals and occupancy limits

A buyer who wants to run stays at your address will meet city rules. Under City Code Section 36-473, a short-term rental is any stay shorter than 30 consecutive days, and it must be registered and carry a city license. A Type 1 license covers a home where the operator lives and needs an annual business license. A Type 2 covers a home the operator does not live in, within single-family and townhouse districts, and needs a permit plus a neighborhood meeting. Two Type 2 homes cannot stand within 500 feet of each other.

The Type 2 application costs $715 for planning review and $30 for inspection, plus the business license. Zoning also caps unrelated occupants at three in single-family and townhouse districts and four in multifamily districts. Suggest the buyer confirm with the city that the property qualifies before the offer goes firm.

Frequently asked questions

What day is Springfield property tax due?

December 31. After that date the county's 2025 notice described a 9 percent penalty plus 2 percent interest, and mailed checks need a postmark of December 31 or earlier.

Which phone number reaches the Springfield tax collector?

The Greene County Collector answers at (417) 868-4036 about payments, and the Assessor at (417) 868-4101 about values. The collection counter is in Room 109 of the Historic Courthouse.

Does Greene County split the tax bill between buyer and seller?

No. The Collector does not divide bills, so the closing company usually credits the seller's share to the buyer. Check the settlement statement.

When can I dispute my Springfield value?

Appeals go to the Board of Equalization, and the form is due to the County Clerk by the second Monday in July. The next reassessment arrives in 2027.

When does Greene County auction delinquent property?

On the fourth Monday of August, at 10 a.m. in Room 212 of the Historic Courthouse. Parcels owing at least two years on May 1 qualify.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Independence property tax?

Get My Cash Offer →

Who sends an Independence property tax bill

The City of Independence does not bill real estate tax. Jackson County does, through two departments: Assessment sets the value, and Collection mails the bill and takes the money. Independence owners can pay at the Historic Truman Courthouse, 112 W Lexington Ave, Suite 114, or at the Jackson County Courthouse in Kansas City. Both open at 8:00 a.m. and close at 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, except county holidays.

Collection answers at (816) 881-3232 and Collections@jacksongov.org. To fix a name or mailing address on a real property account, phone Assessment at 816-881-3530. A change of address filed with the post office or the Missouri DMV never reaches the tax account. Phone lines run long in November and December, so email or the online account lookup may be quicker for simple questions.

Deadline and ways to pay

The tax year 2026 deadline is December 31, 2026. In the prior cycle the county printed bills in early November and finished mailing on December 12. Owners with no bill by December 8 are told to call, and the county warns that a bill that never came is no defense. A check needs a USPS postmark dated December 31 or earlier. The county suggests mailing days early because post office drop boxes sometimes stamp the next day.

The drop box at the south door of the Truman Courthouse locks at midnight on the last day, and cash does not belong in it. Extra Saturday morning hours were offered before the 2025 deadline, so check the Collection page for any new schedule.

Jackson County online payment charges
Payment typeCharge
Any online payment$2.00 flat
E-check (ACH)plus $1.25
Debit or credit cardplus 2.75%
Check or money orderMade out to Jackson County Collector, with the account number

The county says it keeps none of these charges, which go to the payment processor. The online system stops at 11:40 p.m. on December 31.

How a sale affects the bill

Jackson County treats the tax as a lien that follows the real estate, so a buyer inherits any unpaid real estate tax. Buyer and seller commonly prorate the year at closing, and a closing company may pay whatever is due if it knows the amount. As a rule nobody pays the Collector on the day of sale.

  • A buyer who gets a credit at closing should confirm it is meant for the coming tax bill.
  • The new bill may still go out in the seller's name until the buyer reports ownership and an address to the Assessor.
  • Homes with escrow accounts need the bill forwarded to the lender.

Check the parcel at payments.jacksongov.org before you list. Prior-year balances land on the current statement as one lump, so keep last year's bill if you need the breakdown.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Contesting a value

The Board of Equalization accepts filings from May 1 through mid-July each year. After that the window is shut until the next cycle. The Board meets at 1300 Washington in Kansas City, and owners who have filed can withdraw in writing at any time.

Appeals for 2026 will not change this year's statement. Jackson County says recalculation of 2026 appeals and stipulations is paused until January 2027, so pay the full 2026 amount by December 31, 2026. Any overpayment comes back as an automatic refund, with no protest needed. Partial payments on real estate are accepted but cannot be made online, and interest and fees still apply to the unpaid remainder.

The State Tax Commission is the next level and runs its own online application. An owner who signed the Assessor's stipulation has closed the Board case and cannot go on to the Commission.

Independence housing snapshot

Independence sits on the south bank of the Missouri River, mostly in Jackson County with a small piece in Clay County. The 2020 census counted 123,011 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 121,675. There are 51,477 households, 60.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied, the median owned home is valued at $172,900, median gross rent is $1,109 and median household income is $60,339.

Independence, Blue Springs, Fort Osage and Raytown each have school district territory inside the city, so buyers ask which district a particular street falls under. The parcel record answers that.

Evidence for a future appeal

Where a charter county's valuation came from a computer-assisted method, RSMo 137.115 says the assessor must back it with appraisal-based findings and the prices of at least three comparable sales within a mile.

If you expect to challenge a value later, start collecting your own proof now. The Board's appeal page lists certified appraisals, sale contracts and settlement statements, repair estimates and, for income property, rent rolls and leases. A real estate agent's opinion does not qualify, and evidence shown on a phone or tablet will not be considered at the hearing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If you are paying close to the deadline

Order matters in the last week of December. An online payment is the fastest proof, since the system runs until 11:40 p.m. on December 31. A mailed check is judged by its postmark, and the post office is the weak point, because a drop box can stamp the next day. In person, the Truman Courthouse counter closes at 5:00 p.m., while the drop box stays open until midnight but is no place for cash.

Lines at the counter and on the phone are longest in November and December, so people who only need to confirm a balance or print a statement are better off using the account lookup or sending an email to Collections@jacksongov.org.

Escrow accounts and lenders

If a lender pays your taxes from escrow, the bill still needs to reach the lender, and a seller should not assume that happened on its own. Send the statement on, or ask the servicer to confirm it has the current bill. After a sale, the buyer's lender will want the same document, so keep a copy.

A buyer who receives a credit at closing for the seller's share should check that the money is set aside for the coming bill. Since the new bill may still be addressed to the seller, the buyer should report ownership and a mailing address to Assessment rather than wait for the county to catch up.

Selling an Independence house with tax questions

Phone Collection at (816) 881-3232 and ask whether any prior year is open on your parcel. Tell Assessment at 816-881-3530 if the owner's name or mailing address needs correcting, since the post office and the DMV will not pass that along. Give the title company the current statement so it can prorate the year.

If a lien, a tenant or a repair list is slowing a conventional sale, a cash buyer can close without a lender's appraisal, and the tax balance is paid from the proceeds at closing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Which office collects Independence property tax?

Jackson County's Collection Department, at the Historic Truman Courthouse in Independence or the Kansas City courthouse. Call (816) 881-3232.

What is the payment deadline for tax year 2026?

December 31, 2026. Mailed payments need that postmark or an earlier one, and the online system accepts payments until 11:40 p.m. that night.

Do buyers or sellers settle the Independence tax bill?

They usually prorate the year at closing, and a closing company may pay any amount already due. The buyer is liable for unpaid real estate tax because it follows the property.

Can a pending appeal lower the 2026 bill before it is due?

No. Recalculations are suspended until January 2027, so pay the whole 2026 bill by December 31 and a refund follows automatically if the value drops.

What fee applies to online tax payments in Independence?

A $2.00 fee per transaction, plus $1.25 for e-checks or 2.75 percent for cards. The county says it receives none of these fees.
